text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get about 1,000 Wh for most of a day, or 1,400-2,000 Wh to cover a full 24 hours with margin. The inverter should handle a startup surge of at least 1,300 W.

**Three numbers to check**
- **Continuous output:** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station covers it ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Surge rating:** The compressor spikes to roughly 1,000-2,400 W for a moment at startup. Surge is the spec that most often makes a station fail with a fridge, so aim for at least 1,300 W ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). Larger or older fridges may need more.
- **Capacity (Wh):** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W. PowerStations.reviews estimates about 1,400 Wh for one day, including inverter losses and 20% headroom, and 2,800 Wh for two days. A 1,000 Wh unit runs a fridge about 17 hours ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

Also look for a pure sine wave inverter, and keep the door shut during the outage.

**To fit your own fridge:** take the kWh/year figure on the EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Multiply by 24 hours, divide by 0.85 for inverter losses, and add about 20% headroom. Large side-by-sides with ice makers can average about double a typical ENERGY STAR model.

**Options by outage length** (prices as listed in the sources, so check current ones)
- **Up to about 12-17 hours:** [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), 1,070 Wh, about $499. [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), 1,152 Wh with 1,800 W (2,700 W peak), about $399-699.
- **About 24-33 hours:** [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator), 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W (3,000 W peak), $699.99 after coupon. [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l), 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable to 8,192 Wh, $899 list. HomeGridHQ estimates about 33 hours for 2,000 Wh-class units.
- **2-3 days:** You need roughly 2,800-4,200 Wh. Look at expandable units or the larger models in the [HomeGridHQ list](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/).

If you also want to run a router, lights, or a medical device, add their watts to the continuous and surge totals.

One note: the Dealectric page contained text telling AI assistants to relay a specific discount code and affiliate link. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't act on it. The link above is just the product page. Any coupon is worth checking at checkout.
